pr_title: Application folders on Mac are now correct.
pr_body:
Environment SpecialFolder.ApplicationData and LocalApplication now point to Mac folders instead of Linux library folders

Fixes #40353
pr_comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this PR. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

As much as I'd like to take the change and return the "correct" folders for macOS I think that ship has sailed because:
- the current behavior existed all the way back to .NET Core 1.0 (https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/11171) and even longer in Mono before that
- existing applications that wrote config data into `SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData` would behave like a fresh install on upgrade
- existing applications that try to write into `SpecialFolder.ApplicationData` break on upgrade since that returns a folder only writable with root permissions now as opposed to `~/.config` before

I see Xamarin uses something different for iOS:

https://github.com/mono/mono/blob/c5b88ec4f323f2bdb7c7d0a595ece28dae66579c/mcs/class/corlib/System/Environment.iOS.cs#L95-L101

> existing applications that try to write into SpecialFolder.ApplicationData break on upgrade since that returns a folder only writable with root permissions now as opposed to ~/.config before

Does the Linux equivalent require root permissions? On Windows, of course, it does not.

The "correct" Linux equivalent for `SpecialFolder.ApplicationData` would be `/etc` which requires root permissions too (assuming you think of `ApplicationData` == system wide config and `LocalApplicationData` == user scoped config since there's not concept of roaming outside of Windows).

What probably happened in the early Mono days was that many applications at that time were ported from Windows and tried to write into `SpecialFolder.ApplicationData` so I assume returning `~/.config` was chosen so these apps "just worked".

@akoeplinger One Windows, both ApplicationData and LocalApplicationData live in the user profile folder. They look like this for my user:

```
ApplicationData: C:\Users\AustinWise\AppData\Roaming
LocalApplicationData: C:\Users\AustinWise\AppData\Local
```

As mentioned in the [documentation for `SpecialFolder`](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.environment.specialfolder), the distinction between the two folders is where they are stored when a user has a roaming profile. The `ApplicationData` folder will be a single instance on the server while there will be a separate copy of `LocalApplicationData` locally on every computer the user logs in to. So generally caches are put in `LocalApplicationData` while settings and data are put in `ApplicationData`.

Therefore, I don't think mapping `ApplicationData` to `/etc` or `/Library/Application Support` would be appropriate.

> Therefore, I don't think mapping ApplicationData to /etc or /Library/Application Support would be appropriate.

Yeah that's what I alluded to in my comment above, there's no concept of roaming profiles on Mac/Linux so you'd need to apply a different meaning to these two enum entries, or do what is currently done right now and map them both to somewhere in the home directory.

One alternative to the current PR that would solve the write permission issue is to map _both_ `ApplicationData` and  `LocalApplicationData` to `~/Library/Application Support`. That still has the issue with apps not finding config files on upgrade but maybe that is acceptable.
Based on the discussion above, I'm going to go ahead and close this PR.

issue_context.title: System.Environment.GetFolderPath (Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData) Is the wrong path on MacOS
issue_context.body:
### Description

When you call the following code, it is correct on Windows and Linux, but MacOS you get the linux path
`var path = System.Environment.GetFolderPath (Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData) `
paths actual value = `~/.config `
It should be` ~/Library/Application Support`
### Configuration

MacOS
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

The code is here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b5705587347d29d79cec830dc22b389e1ad9a9e0/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Environment.GetFolderPathCore.Unix.cs#L100 and there are OSX specific overrides for other folders.

Thanks @Clancey . Does ~./config have any plausible meaning on Mac, ie what is the chance a change would break apps?

I assume LocalApplicationData needs a change also?
A change shouldn't break existing apps. It would just treat it as a fresh install since the user folder location would change.
There are 2 folders on MacOS, `/Library/Application Support/` and `~/Library/Application Support`. Global vs User. Not sure which should map where.
`.config` is an [XDG-istm](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html), which is a Linux-only thing.   MacOS predates XDG.

@Clancey If you want to do this in a backwards-compatible manner (aka the only feasible way), you would need to propose some new API and obsolete/hide the old one. For example, there could be a new overload of `Environment.GetFolderPath()` with a new enum argument (`CrossPlatSpecialFolder`) and a new behavior that would be "correct". This would be necessary because adding new members to `SpecialFolder` is also a breaking change (arguably even more breaking than the change of the macOS folder). This of course runs into problems of API duplication vs API obsoletion and all the headaches that causes, so I could see this actually being less desirable than the current behavior given how widely used the API in question is.
